summary: This Wikipedia-derived note surveys communications in Somalia across radio, satellite internet, television and postal services. It covers Radio Mogadishu's history, the growth and decline of satellite internet via Dalkom Somalia, other Mogadishu radio stations, the relaunch of Somali National Television in 2011, and the government's phased plan to rebuild the national postal service with UPU support.
one_line: Overview of Somalia's radio, satellite internet, television and postal communications, including post-civil-war rebuilding efforts.
key_facts: Radio Mogadishu was established during the colonial period and initially broadcast news in Somali and Italian.
Radio Mogadishu was modernized with Russian assistance following Somalia's independence in 1960.
Radio Mogadishu closed down in the early 1990s due to the civil war and was officially re-opened in the early 2000s by the Transitional National Government.
As of 2009, Internet via satellite had a steady growth rate of 10% to 15% per year.

Dalkom Somalia provided internet over satellite and offered inexpensive bandwidth through its internet backbone, whereas bandwidth ordinarily cost customers from $2,500 to $3,000 per month through major international providers.
In total, over 300 local satellite terminals were available across Somalia, linked to teleports in Europe and Asia.
In 2010 the Shabelle Media Network was awarded the Media of the Year prize by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), a Paris-based journalism organisation.
In total, about one short-wave and ten private FM radio stations broadcast from Mogadishu.
Somali National Television began experimental broadcasts on March 18, 2011, under the Ministry of Information of the Transitional Federal Government.
Somali National Television was officially re-launched on April 4, 2011, after a 20-year hiatus, and broadcasts 24 hours a day.
Phase I of the Somali Post reconstruction plan includes rebuilding the General Post Office and establishing 16 branch offices in the capital and 17 in regional bases.
As of March 2012, Somalia had re-established its membership with the Universal Postal Union (UPU).
Phase II involves the construction of 718 postal outlets from 2014 to 2016.
Phase III is slated to begin in 2017, with the objective of creating 897 postal outlets by 2022.
On 1 November 2013, international postal services for Somalia officially resumed.
